original_card.question: Can one precisely specified helper-mixing word satisfy a replacement for the inherited H2/K interface?
methods: Derive a replacement interface lemma and price its implementation.
Seek an exact dirty-input or chronological-cut counterexample to the proposed replacement.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient.

first_step.inspect: Compare the two false H2/K flags with the unchanged paid profile in its README.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Write one replacement H2/K implication for a single helper-star operation, then try to falsify it on dirty inputs.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A legitimate replacement could admit a cheaper bit circuit; scalar savings alone do not alter the selected moment.
allowed_variations: Choose one helper-star or quartet instance; narrow to one boundary implication.
scope_change_triggers: Changing only source count or scalar addition count without an interface argument.

actual_scope: Five-step directed cyclic helper basis changes applied after the pinned R439 helper preparation, with injection J0 H1^-1 and reverse restoration, exhaustively priced on all five-subsets of the top 20 overlap-ranked helper coordinates.
scope_change_reason: The originally suggested helper-star/quartet instances already have source-pinned constructions and searches in main; a fresh overlap scan found no current claim for a five-helper cyclic sweep. The second eligible bit task is covered broadly by fresh PRs #1333 and #1662. This changes the mixing topology and checks the exact dirty-boundary identity for the new word rather than auditing the predecessor.
bottleneck_link: The resulting word retains the same rank/copy/frame profile, so it changes no recursive moment or kappa and cannot unbind the selected complex side. It is a fully charged local bit-circuit reduction that may provide a lower-cost R439 implementation if the inherited supplier and hosting obligations are later accepted.
stop_rule: Exhaust exactly 15,504 five-helper supports among the overlap-ranked top 20 and all 120 directed cyclic sweeps per support; certify the selected maximum-saving candidate under the exact D/full-word, paid-profile, exporter and precision checks. Stop without searching other support cutoffs, cycle lengths, target bases or supplier assembly.
evidence: SEARCH-RESULT.json records all 1,860,480 candidates and the 109-ADD optimistic ceiling. CANDIDATE.json.gz is the deterministic 12-ADD winner. verify.py checks source pins, the 661-coordinate dirty endpoint, the complete R439 word in both directions, paid profile, exporter and five boundary failure controls.
author: Cinna Davis (@1337isnot1337)
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in mathematical scoping, derivation, search implementation, exact checking and package writing. No independent human review is claimed.

open_questions.question: Can a six-helper cyclic basis change lower the same R439 injection cost beyond the five-helper result?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A longer cycle could expose multi-column cancellations that a single five-cycle cannot realize.
open_questions.first_step: Compute the exact six-column rank lower bound and full six-edge preparation/restoration charge on a seed-selected overlap-ranked support family before enumerating cyclic words.
open_questions.blocked_by: A positive fully charged ceiling and a bounded support family whose exact endpoint and precision can be replayed.
